transcript:
[00:00] So what's been happening with your hands?
[00:04] For about six months now my knuckles and my wrists have been swollen and sore, and in the mornings they're stiff for about an hour and a half.
[00:15] Okay. Any psoriasis, scaly patches on the skin, elbows, scalp?
[00:19] No, nothing like that.
[00:21] Any bowel problems, Crohn's or colitis?
[00:24] No.
[00:25] Does anyone in the family have arthritis?
[00:28] My mother had rheumatoid arthritis, she was on injections for it.
[00:33] Any gout in the family? No? And do your fingers go white in the cold?
[00:38] No, not really.
[00:40] Do you smoke?
[00:41] I gave up about five years ago.
[00:44] What are you taking at the moment?
[00:46] Just the naproxen, 500 milligrams twice a day, and an omeprazole in the morning, 20.
[00:53] Any allergies to medicines?
[00:55] Penicillin, I came out in a rash.
[01:20] Right, examining you now. Tender and swollen right second and third MCPs, swollen left wrist, tender left wrist too. Knees are fine. Range of movement at the shoulders is normal.
[01:41] Your bloods from the GP showed a CRP of 24 and the rheumatoid factor was positive.
[01:50] So I'm going to order an anti-CCP and the routine bloods, and X-rays of both hands and feet.
[01:58] I'd like to start you on methotrexate, starting at ten milligrams once a week, with folic acid, and I'll give you the leaflet about pregnancy and contraception.
[02:10] I'll also give you an injection of Depo-Medrone into the thigh today to settle things down.
[02:16] We'll see you back in three months.
summary: Six-month history of pain and swelling of the knuckles and wrists with approximately 90 minutes of early morning stiffness.
